title: Projects
text:
MindTheAI (CMD-F 2026)A Chrome extension for responsible AI use that protects sensitive information, flags unreliable sources and nudges users to rethink unnecessary prompts. Won the 1Password security prize.Hackathon · Chrome extension · Responsible AI · Security · March 2026


Overview
MindTheAI is a Chrome extension built at the CMD-F 2026 hackathon to help people use AI tools more thoughtfully and more safely.
What it does

Password protection, so sensitive details stay out of AI prompts
Removes personal data and prompt filler before a prompt is sent
Flags unreliable sources
Usage reminders that nudge users to rethink unnecessary prompts
Helps users understand the impacts of AI usage

Result
Won the 1Password sponsor prize for the best integration of security practices into a coding project. Winners received $100 and 1Password subscriptions.



Devpost · Repository




The Daily Grind (CMD-F 2025)Built a coffee-chat conversation starter in 24 hours that won the Social track and placed 3rd overall among 50+ projects.Hackathon · Team project · Hackathon · March 2025







The popup where users add details to get conversation topics




‹


›


Overview
A 24-hour hackathon with 200+ participants and 50+ projects. Our coffee-chat conversation starter helps people break the ice: users add a few details in a popup and get useful conversation topics.
Result
Winner of the Social track and 3rd place overall. After presenting to 7 judges, we were invited to present to the whole hackathon community of 250+ people. Winners received $200 and had the project featured on the cmd-f website.


See it on Devpost




DataFest Statistical Analysis (ASA 2025)A fully reproducible 48-hour analysis with a Bayesian model, delivered with a dashboard, demo video and slides, all built in Quarto.Statistics · Bayesian modelling · EDA · Quarto · Hackathon


Overview
A 48-hour American Statistical Association DataFest competition, completed with a team of 3.
Approach
Extensive exploratory data analysis followed by a Bayesian model. Everything was built in Quarto so the full analysis can be reproduced from start to finish.
Deliverables
A data dashboard, a demonstration video and presentation slides.


Presentation · Repository




Statistical Research Consulting (Capstone)Real client work in medical research: analyzed changes after glaucoma surgery in R and presented the findings to the client and at a poster session.Statistics · R · Study design · Model selection · Consulting







Our final poster board




‹


›


Overview
Consulting work for a client in medical research, analyzing changes after glaucoma eye surgery (STAT 450).
Process

Presented regularly to Professor Rodolfo Lourenzutti to keep the work high-quality and reliable
Met with the client and gave technical oral presentations to the class
Presented the findings at a poster session
Produced written reports, a code repository and visualizations in R and GitHub

What I learned
Study design, model selection and how to communicate statistics clearly to a non-statistical audience.

Weather Extremes ResearchSummer research assistantship (NSERC USRA) using time series analysis in Python and R to find patterns in Canadian floods, droughts and wildfires.Research · Python · R · Time series · EDA · Quarto


Overview
Research assistant at UBC in summer 2024, funded by an NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award and supervised by Professors Harry Joe and Natalia Nolde.
What I did
I explored Canadian weather data on floods, droughts and wildfires, using exploratory analysis and time series methods to look for patterns. I analyzed research papers, presented my work weekly and used Quarto for presentations.
Status
I’m cleaning up the code to publish it in a public repository.





Library Attendance Dashboard (DSCI 320)An interactive Python dashboard on San Francisco library attendance, built with two teammates to answer four research questions.Analytics · Python · Data visualization · Interactive dashboards







Custom dashboard for DSCI 320: Data Visualization




‹


›


Overview
With two teammates, I built a fully interactive dashboard exploring attendance at libraries in the San Francisco area.
The brief
The course asked for inventive visualizations that answer 4 questions. The dashboard includes toggle options that the screenshot doesn’t show.






wordplayr, an R packageA documented R package with a vignette and a pkgdown website that finds patterns in word lists.Engineering · R · Roxygen · pkgdown · Vignettes







Preview of the package website




‹


›


Overview
wordplayr finds patterns in a list of words: average word length, common starting letters, frequent vowel sounds and more.
Why I built it
I’ve kept a list of my favorite words for years and wanted to understand why I like them. (They most often start with “C”.)
What’s included
A README with install instructions, a vignette, a package website and Roxygen documentation.
Repository · Website

title: About
text:
I’m a data modernization consultant working toward a career in data engineering. I graduated from the University of British Columbia in May 2025 with a major in Statistics and a minor in Data Science, including a semester at the University of Oslo.
Day to day I work with Databricks, Microsoft Fabric and Power BI in Python, R, SQL and DAX. I’m interested in data engineering, Azure consulting, and analytics and experimentation roles.
My statistics background shows up in my work: I’ve done a research consulting capstone, a research assistantship in climate extremes, and hackathons where we shipped under pressure. Outside of work, I enjoy running, climbing, and crocheting.
